description: ghostty/include/ghostty.h:1136 declares void ghostty_surface_free_text(ghostty_surface_t, ghostty_text_s*) but ghostty/src/apprt/embedded.zig:1725 exports fn ghostty_surface_free_text(ptr: *Text). Callers follow the header and pass (surface, &text); on arm64 the callee reads x0 = surface. Two consequences: (1) the text buffer allocated by readTextLocked via dumpTextLocked(global.alloc) is never freed - measured ~4.9 blocks/request, avg 21KB, ~100KB per surface.read_text in a dev build under MallocStackLogging, stack confirms heap.CAllocator.alloc under TerminalController.readTerminalTextBase64; (2) Text.deinit runs on the Surface reinterpreted as Text and may call global.alloc.free on a pointer/len read from arbitrary struct offsets - benign only while that offset is null. Affects every c11 caller: TerminalController.swift readSelectionText, GhosttyTerminalView.swift:5000 and :5241. Upstream bug in the ghostty fork (submodule 7604624d), not c11 header drift - the header ships from ghostty itself. Fix belongs in the submodule (make the export take the surface param the header promises), which per CLAUDE.md means a push to Stage-11-Agentics/ghostty plus the build-ghosttykit checksum cycle, and is shared with cmux/upstream so the operator should decide where it lands. Found while validating C11-211.
title: ghostty_surface_free_text ABI mismatch: header takes (surface, text), Zig export takes (text) — every terminal text read leaks its buffer
